items.prompt:
To come PREPARED to a book discussion, you should:
A) read the book and bring ideas
B) show up with nothing
C) read a different book
items.answer: A) read the book and bring ideas

steps: Get ready ahead. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) read the book and bring ideas

items.prompt:
When a classmate is talking, you should:
A) listen
B) talk over them
C) leave

steps: Listen to others. Key is A.

items.prompt:
If you don't understand a point, you should:
A) ask a question
B) say nothing and stay confused
C) change the subject

steps: Ask to understand. Key is A.

items.prompt:
A classmate says, 'The hero was brave.' You say, 'Yes, and she was also kind.' You are:
A) building on their idea
B) ignoring them
C) changing the topic

steps: Adding to their point. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Which shows you are following discussion RULES?
A) Taking turns and listening
B) Talking the whole time
C) Looking at your phone

steps: Rules of discussion. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Staying on the discussion's subject is called staying on:
A) topic
B) time
C) your seat

Which response BUILDS on a classmate's idea the best?
A) 'I think the wolf was scary. He also tricked the pigs, which shows he was clever.'
B) 'Anyway, I like soccer.'
C) 'No, you're wrong.'
items.answer: A) 'I think the wolf was scary. He also tricked the pigs, which shows he was clever.'

steps: Connects and adds a point. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) 'I think the wolf was scary. He also tricked the pigs, which shows he was clever.'

items.prompt:
Why is it important to come prepared to a discussion?
A) So you have ideas to share and can follow along
B) So you can talk first
C) It is not important
items.answer: A) So you have ideas to share and can follow along

steps: Preparation helps you contribute. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) So you have ideas to share and can follow along
